title: A GRA-Enhanced Cloud AI Framework for Petabyte-Scale Multi-Tenant Environments: Multivariate Classification for Credit Card Fraud Detection and Adaptive Risk Analytics
venue: International Journal of Engineering & Extended Technologies Research
tldr: Integrating Grey Relational Analysis as a lightweight relational signature with ML ensembles in a cloud-native, multi-tenant architecture improves credit-card fraud detection AUC by 3-6 points while reducing compute utilization by 35-60 percent.
problem_and_motivation: Modern payment platforms must process billions of petabyte-scale events per day across multiple tenants with different risk profiles, yet traditional classifiers trained in isolation struggle with scale, heterogeneity, and continual fraud pattern shifts. Existing fraud detection systems rely on engineered aggregates or sequence encoders without integrating lightweight similarity measures that could improve interpretability and reduce compute overhead. There is little published work integrating Grey Relational Analysis as a first-stage relational signature in cloud-native, multi-tenant, petabyte-scale fraud detection pipelines.
approach: Design a multi-tiered architecture coupling GRA preprocessing with streaming and batch ML pipelines for petabyte-scale transaction data.
Compute GRA relational signatures per sliding window (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d) comparing transaction sequences against per-card, tenant, and global baselines.
Use GRA signatures simultaneously as a prefilter to reduce candidate sets, as direct ML input features, and as analyst explanation attributes.
Construct a hybrid ensemble with gradient-boosted decision trees for fast scoring and temporal graph neural networks for complex pattern detection.
Apply isotonic regression or Platt scaling for probability calibration, then fuse outputs via weighted averaging based on tenant confidence and GRA-derived novelty.
Implement cost-sensitive learning, focal loss, and drift monitors with GRA-signature-based early drift indicators to handle class imbalance and concept drift.
Integrate semi-supervised label propagation across the transaction graph with strict tenant-policy constraints to prevent cross-tenant leakage.
Evaluate on synthetic transaction corpora and benchmark datasets using ablation studies comparing GRA-only, ML-only, and combined configurations.
Use lakehouse storage, locality-aware SSD caching, and tenant-partitioned data layouts to achieve sub-300ms median streaming scoring latency at petabyte scale.
findings: num: GRA prefilter reduced transactions forwarded to heavyweight inference by 40-70% with less than 5% loss of true fraud events.
num: Compute utilization for heavy models decreased by 35-60% per hour through GRA candidate filtering.
num: Combined GRA plus ensemble improved ROC AUC by 3-6 percentage points over the best baseline across most scenarios.
num: Precision at top k (precision@1000) improved by 5-12% with GRA integration.
num: False positives for low-risk tenant groups reduced by up to 18% when tenant risk policies were applied.
num: End-to-end streaming scoring latencies met sub-300ms median SLOs at hundreds of thousands of transactions per second.
num: GRA signatures served as early drift indicators, reducing model degradation time compared to baseline periodic retraining.
GRA relational drift scores on specific feature groups provided interpretable cues for analyst triage of anomaly types.
Tenants with sparse labeled fraud data benefited most from GRA unsupervised signals while richly labeled tenants relied more on supervised models.

definitions.definition: Grey Relational Analysis, a similarity measure from grey systems theory producing bounded relational coefficients between sequences.
Gradient-Boosted Decision Tree, a fast ensemble model used for instant scoring on candidate transaction sets.
Temporal Graph Neural Network, a deep model consuming sequence embeddings and graph context to detect complex fraud patterns.
Merchant Category Code, a numerical code assigned to a merchant by the card network.
Personally Identifiable Information, sensitive data such as PANs and customer identifiers requiring tokenization.
Service Level Objective, defined thresholds for latency, availability, and model staleness in operational systems.
Area Under the Curve, a metric measuring classification quality of the fraud detection model.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, a model-agnostic framework for producing human-readable feature importance explanations.
Primary Account Number, the card number requiring tokenization at ingestion for privacy protection.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a novel integration of Grey Relational Analysis as a first-class computational primitive within cloud-native fraud detection pipelines. It demonstrates that lightweight relational signatures can serve triple duty as candidate prefilters, ML input features, and analyst explanation attributes. The multi-tenant architecture provides a blueprint for balancing per-tenant risk policies, compute cost, and detection quality at petabyte scale. Empirical evaluation on synthetic workloads shows measurable improvements in AUC, precision, and operational efficiency when GRA is added to modern ML ensembles. The work also addresses practical concerns including drift detection, semi-supervised label propagation, and privacy-preserving collaborative learning.
directly_justifies: GRA prefilter reduced transactions forwarded to heavyweight inference by 40-70% with less than 5% fraud event loss.
Combined GRA plus ensemble improved ROC AUC by 3-6 percentage points over the best baseline.
False positives for low-risk tenant groups reduced by up to 18% with tenant risk policies.
GRA signatures changed measurably during simulated concept drift, serving as early drift indicators.
End-to-end streaming scoring met sub-300ms median latency at hundreds of thousands of transactions per second.
limits: Evaluation relies on synthetic transaction corpora rather than production-scale real-world data.
GRA alone cannot detect sophisticated adversarial mimicry patterns without deeper models.
Per-tenant model governance and versioning challenges at scale are acknowledged but not fully resolved.
Cost-benefit analyses are scenario-dependent and may not generalize to all tenant profiles.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) was flagged as most relevant: 8.B receives high relevance because GRA is the core anomaly detection algorithm applied to financial transaction data, 8.A receives medium because the focus is fraud detection rather than personal finance anomalies, and 8.C receives medium because the GRA baseline strategy (per-card, tenant, global references) parallels cold-start detection approaches. Domain 14 (ML deployment) was flagged: 14.B receives medium for the comprehensive cloud ML serving architecture, and 14.A receives low for synthetic transaction corpus usage. Domain 10 (Privacy) received low relevance for tokenization and encryption discussion. Domains 1-3 (Filipino demographics, culturally specific practices, expense categorization) were considered and rejected as the paper has no connection to personal finance demographics or budgeting. Domains 5-7 (behavioral profiles, predictive modeling, budgeting strategies) were rejected because the paper addresses fraud classification rather than personal finance behavioral modeling or budget recommendation. Domain 9 (mobile-first design) was rejected as the paper describes cloud infrastructure not mobile UX. Domain 11 (engagement dynamics) was rejected with no relevant content. Domain 12 (evaluation frameworks) was considered but deemed low relevance since the paper's evaluation is domain-specific to fraud detection. Domain 13 (savings/debt management) was rejected as entirely unrelated.

limitations: Evaluation uses synthetic transaction corpora designed to mimic real distributions but may not fully capture production complexity. [unacknowledged]
GRA alone cannot replace deep pattern detection for sophisticated adversaries who deliberately mimic tenant baselines.
Per-tenant model variants and transfer learning introduce governance challenges including versioning and cross-tenant fairness monitoring.
Cross-tenant graph propagation risks data leakage unless strict policy and cryptographic controls are enforced.
Engineering and storage overhead from caching layers, metadata services, and tenant orchestration increases operational cost.
